items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: we had some, uh, stuff from Benny Hall. We used to buy all our stuff from that, so we called that the Tip Seas, yeah.

ctx.x: that's right. That was, that was before Sidney Desmond, I mean Sidney Desmond, because there was, there was a fella named John Morell, banjo player. He had a job at the La Vida, as a jitney dance. That's right. And, um, and that band was, the leader was John Morell, the banjo player, and, uh, Lee Collins on trumpet. Thereto Poinnell on alto and David Jones on tenor. Yeah. Uh, Joe Rovershaw on piano, uh, and, uh, Albert Martin, I think, the drummer. Oh, Albert Martin. Yeah. On drum, and I took John Morell's play.…
this damp weather, see? Everybody was kind of white. And there wasn't one named Tip Easy or something? Tip Easy. Yeah, like, well, we had all,

I was doing probation day, and we had some, uh, stuff from Benny Hall. We used to buy all our stuff from that, so we called that the Tip Seas, yeah. Yeah. And in that session, now, Albert, um, Martin had gone with, um, a fellow named Don Albert. Yeah. Because he came through town to Texas, and he had, um, he took members, they took fellows out of three or four bands around here, you see? And I was supposed to go over them, too, but I had already had this offer to go with sitting Desvino on the boat, you see? And,…
